summary.name: Continuous deployment
summary.one_liner: Wikipedia article describing continuous deployment, a software engineering practice where changes that pass automated testing are released to production automatically without manual approval.
use_cases: Understanding how to automatically release code to production
Deciding whether to move from continuous delivery to continuous deployment
Releasing features gradually with feature toggles
Planning automated testing needs for frequent releases
summary.what_it_does: The page explains continuous deployment as a software engineering approach where functionality is delivered frequently through automated deployments, with no manual approval step. It contrasts this with continuous delivery, where changes are ready to deploy but not actually deployed. It describes motivations such as faster release cycles, easier bug isolation through small changes, and quicker customer feedback. It also covers challenges, including the need for high test coverage, real-time monitoring, and a DevOps culture shift. An example describes deploying a new microservice version and retiring the old one after in-flight requests drain.
notable: Distinguishes continuous deployment from continuous delivery: deployment is fully automated, while delivery stops short of production release
Uses feature toggles and dark launches to deploy code months before public release
Requires a much higher standard of automated testing because test quality determines release reliability
Describes microservice example: instantiate new version, retire old one after in-flight requests drain
caveats: Continuous deployment requires significant investment in test coverage, real-time monitoring, and CI pipelines
Constantly changing software can create a learning curve for customers
Cultural shift for developers accustomed to traditional release cycles; often requires a proven DevOps process
